Preliminary information regarding accident in question was received at PS Lajpat Nagar vide DD No. 93A dated 24.01.2022 vide PCR call in respect of an accident, upon receipt of which ASI Ashok Kumar alongwith Ct. Naresh Kumar proceeded to the spot of accident in front of Axis Bank, Metro Pillar no. 15, BRT Road, New Delhi, where they were informed that the injured has already been rushed to hospital.
Any offending vehicle was not found at the spot.

In the meanwhile, GD No.4A in respect of MLC from AIIMS Trauma Center of patient Narayan Dutt, another MLC for Avinash Khare and yet another MLC of patient Viom was received, in pursuance to which, ASI Ashok Kumar along-with Ct. Naresh Kumar went to AIIMS Trauma Center and collected the MLCs.
Eye-witness Manish Kumar also met them in the hospital, whose statement was recorded.

He informed that on 24.01.2022 at about 8.30p.m., while he along-with his colleague Narayan Dutt, employed as Salesman in Monte Carlo Showroom, Lajpat Nagar-II, were walking towards their rented room in Kotla Mubarakpur, that a speeding and rashly driven Bullet Motorcycle bearing registration No.
DL3SEN 1060 (Black Colour) with two riders coming from the side of Moolchand Flyover impacted his colleague due to which, he as well as the motorcyclists fell down and received injuries.
He also stated that the motorcyclists identified themselves as Viom and Avinash.
He also informed that the bike was being driven by Avinash whereas Viom was the pillion rider.
He also informed that he took the injured/claimant to the hospital and later, the motorcyclists also came to AIIMS Trauma Center for their treatment.
FIR was got registered.
Site Plan was prepared at the instance of the eye-witness.
Statement of Narayan Dutt/claimant/injured was also recorded.
Motorcycle was found to be registered in the name of Avinash Khare, who was examined and he produced the relevant documents of motorcycle.
The motorcycle was found to be uninsured as on the date of accident.
Mechanical inspection of the motorcycle was got conducted.

Upon conclusion of investigation,
respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted for injuring claimant on account of rash and negligent driving of motorcycle on a public way.
DAR was filed by Investigating Officer before this Tribunal.
3. Respondent appeared before the court and copy of DAR was supplied to him.
Reply to DAR was not filed.

4. It was mentioned that he has deposited security amount of Rs.1,00,000/- in the court of Ld. MM at the time of release of vehicle as noted in the order dated 07.11.2022.
5.

i).

OPP.

Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation and if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP iii).

9.
What is required to be ascertained is whether rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle resulted in accident which caused injuries to the claimant.
10. No evidence has been led by any of the parties, therefore issue will be decided on the basis of DAR filed in this matter.
11. FIR was registered on the basis of statement of eye-witness Sh. Mukesh, who was walking with the injured at the time of accident and who took the injured for the medical treatment.
His statement was recorded in the hospital leading to registration of the FIR.
Site Plan was also prepared at his instance.
Site plan reflects that the accident took place not in the middle of the road but on one edge of the road.
Information about the accident was given to police station recorded by PCR call.

Mechanical Inspection of the offending vehicle also shows fresh accidental damage,
corroborating the statement of Mukesh Kumar, the eye- witness and the first informer.
The motorcyclists also received injuries in the accident, therefore, as such, there is no dispute with respect to identification of the offending vehicle or the driver thereof.

Eye-witness Mukesh Kumar specified in his statement recorded by the police that the vehicle was being driven by Avinesh Khare,
whose MLC was collected by IO ASI Ashok Kumar.
No explanation has been rendered by respondent indicative of the circumstances which led to the accident or suggesting that he was not at fault.
It has been categorically stated by the injured on whose statement FIR was registered that the offending motorcycle was speeding and was being rashly driven which led to the accident.
Respondent has also been charge-sheeted of rash and negligent driving on a public way.
There is nothing on record to show any glaring action or inaction on the part of the injured to draw any inference about his contribution to the occurrence of the accident.

It is noted that respondent has not filed any response to the DAR and therefore, there is not even basic denial of any accident or involvement of the offending vehicle or that it was not the result of his negligence.

Considering the documents filed as part of DAR including charge-sheet based primarily upon statement of eye witness and that driver never contested the petition to argue that he was not driving the alleged offending vehicle at the time of accident or that he was driving in normal speed within his lane and that accident is not attributed to his rash driving, with not even a feeble attempt made by respondent/driver to deny or to set up an alternative explanation to the narrative, it is evident that accident happened on account of speedy and rash driving by driver of the offending vehicle.
Issue in hand is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

18. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science.
Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability.
(As observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sidram Vs. The Divisional Manager United India Insurance Company Ltd, SLP (Civil) No. 19277 of 2019).

21. Delineating the damages as pecuniary and non pecuniary, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case of R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt Ltd, 1995 AIR 755, made following observations:
"9....while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.
Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which are capable of being calculated in terms of money; whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

sentences.text:
In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by the claimant:
(i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship,
discomfort, disappointment, frustration and mental stress in life."
22. Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

sentences.text: Following observations are relevant in the context:
"40.General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 5.

The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

23. It is settled proposition of law as held in catena of judgments that "just compensation" should include all elements that would go to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in, before the occurrence of the accident.

Whilst no amount of money or other material compensation can erase the trauma, pain and suffering that a victim undergoes after a serious accident, (or replace the loss of a loved one), monetary compensation is the manner known to law, whereby society assures some measure of restitution to those who survive, and the victims who have to face their lives.
24. As any evidence has not been led, there is nothing to understand the nature of avocation/employment of injured.
There is nothing mentioned about his educational or technical qualification either.
His address has been mentioned to be that of Kotla Mubarakpur, Delhi as per DAR.
In the MLC also, his address is mentioned to be that of Kotla Mubrakpur, Delhi.

It was mentioned by Sh. Mukesh Kumar, eye-witness that Narayan Dutt is his colleage and both of them were employed as a Sales Persons with a Store in Lajpat Nagar and were on their way back to their rental accommodation at Kotla Mubarakpur, Delhi when accident happened.
Even though, Aadhar Card of injured placed on record reflects address of the State of Uttrakhand, however it is evident that he was working for gain in Delhi at the time of accident.
It was mentioned in DAR that injured was earning Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/- per month.
Accordingly, his income is taken to be minimum wages for an unskilled labour as applicable in the State of NCT of Delhi, which was Rs.16,064/- per month.
As per Discharge Summary, injured remained admitted in the hospital for about six days post accident.

He was diagnosed with Right Temporal EDH with Bilateral Temporal Contusions and underwent operative procedure of "Right Temporal Craniotomy"
and later discharged on a good GCS Score.

He was advised regular follow-up,
however any further medical consultation record has not been filed.
Medical bills till the month of March, 2022 have been filed on record, reflecting that he was under active medical treatment.

Considering the nature of injuries and the nature of job and the medical bills filed on record, it is reasonable to presume that injured would not have been able to resume normal working for atleast four months post accident.

Thus, injured suffered loss of income during treatment to the tune of Rs.64,256/-
(Rs.16,064 x 4).

strict rules of evidence are not applicable (support drawn from the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs.

13.
Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent under section 279 & 338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent/driver in causing the accident.
14. It is also settled that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him as observed by Hon'ble High Court of India in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310.
15.
In the present case also, driver/respondent did not enter into the witness box to controvert the claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident.
It is noted that respondent has not filed any response to the DAR and therefore, there is not even basic denial of any accident or involvement of the offending vehicle or that it was not the result of his negligence.
16.
Considering the documents filed as part of DAR including charge-sheet based primarily upon statement of eye witness and that driver never contested the petition to argue that he was not driving the alleged offending vehicle at the time of accident or that he was driving in normal speed within his lane and that accident is not attributed to his rash driving, with not even a feeble attempt made by respondent/driver to deny or to set up an alternative explanation to the narrative, it is evident that accident happened on account of speedy and rash driving by driver of the offending vehicle.
18. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science.
Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability.
(As observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sidram Vs. The Divisional Manager United India Insurance Company Ltd, SLP (Civil) No. 19277 of 2019).
[Support drawn from Govind Ram Yadav vs. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2011)
10 SCC 683] .
20.
22. Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
[See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 :
1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 :
(1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .]
6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence.

23. It is settled proposition of law as held in catena of judgments that "just compensation" should include all elements that would go to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in, before the occurrence of the accident.
Whilst no amount of money or other material compensation can erase the trauma, pain and suffering that a victim undergoes after a serious accident, (or replace the loss of a loved one), monetary compensation is the manner known to law, whereby society assures some measure of restitution to those who survive, and the victims who have to face their lives.
